turns.text: Explain our workforce position in plain terms — pretend I'm a brand-new dean.

Here's the lay of the land for Advanced Manufacturing across your district. Employers around the Bay Area are hiring for about 8,150 of these jobs a year. All 26 colleges in the region together graduate about 3,923 people a year into them — so regional demand runs ahead of regional supply by roughly 4,227 a year. Your district — the three colleges together — produces about 200 of those graduates a year, a little over 5% of the region's total. You run two programs in the sector, Electronics and Electric Technology and Energy Systems Technology, and the sector as a whole spans 49 different occupations. One note on the graduate figures: they're a three-year average of completions, so any single recent year can run a bit above or below.

Simpler: the Bay Area needs about 8,150 advanced-manufacturing workers a year. Every college in the region combined graduates only about 3,900 — leaving a shortfall of roughly 4,200 a year. Your district trains about 200 of them, a small share of the region.
The Bay Area comes up about 4,200 advanced-manufacturing workers short each year, and your district produces roughly 200 of the region's graduates.
